transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I keep getting hit out of nowhere with that scene—my cousin on the pavement. I can hear the shouting and see the lights again, even when I’m just in the church office trying to act normal.
I'm so sorry you went through that. How long ago did this happen to your cousin?
It was two years and three months ago—when my cousin was killed.
Do you find yourself trying to avoid people, places, or situations that remind you of what happened?
Yeah. I take the long way around town so I don’t have to go past the community center or the court. And if someone starts talking about that night, I usually shut it down or find a reason to leave.
Do you find yourself feeling constantly on guard or on edge, as if something bad might happen at any moment?

Yeah. I can’t sit with my back to a door anymore. At church events, I’m always watching people’s hands, the corners of the room, cars slowing down outside, where the nearest exit is. I’m not really paying attention to the people right in front of me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced an exceptionally traumatic event (the violent killing of their cousin) over two years ago. They present with classic triad features of Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD): intrusive re-experiencing (flashbacks/vivid sensory recollections of the scene), deliberate avoidance of trauma-related reminders (routes, places, and conversations), and marked persistent hypervigilance/hyperarousal.

confirmed_symptoms: Involuntary intrusive recollections/flashbacks of the scene where the cousin was killed, including sensory details of shouting and flashing lights
Avoidance of physical locations associated with the event (taking alternative routes to avoid the community center and court)
Avoidance of conversations or reminders of that night
Persistent hypervigilance and scanning for threats (cannot sit with back to doors, monitoring hands, exits, and slowing cars)

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have persisted for two years and three months following the traumatic event
additional_requirements: Trauma involving violent death of a close family member
